messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm about to merge a terraform change that tweaks the inference provisioner scaling policy and hands off secret ownership to the infra team. Before I do, quick ownership + safety check: who currently owns the Vault path `secret/data/inference/provisioner` and are there any consumers we need to notify?

maria: I think the path is currently used by the inference deploy job and the canary scaler. Ownership was initially with platform-security but they handed operational ownership to infra last quarter.

sahil: Noted. We run a cron job that rotates the key monthly. If you change the path, update the CronJob env and the HPA/VPA controller refs.

jen: who from infra will ack? Also any rolling strategy required to avoid throttles? :thinking_face:

alex: @maria can you confirm infra owns it now and whether the rotation job name is `secret-rotator-inference`?

maria: confirmed. infra owns it. rotation job is `secret-rotator-inference` in namespace `infra-tools`.

alex: ok good. The terraform diff is small: just adding an owner tag and a new policy binding to the service account `provisioner-sa`. snippet:

```hcl
resource "vault_policy" "provisioner_rw" {
  name = "provisioner-rw"
  policy = file("policies/provisioner-rw.hcl")
}

resource "vault_kv_secret" "provisioner" {
  path = "secret/data/inference/provisioner"
  data_json = jsonencode({ key = var.provisioner_key })
}

resource "vault_auth_backend_role" "provisioner_role" {
  role_name = "provisioner-role"
  bound_service_account_names = ["provisioner-sa"]
  bound_service_account_namespaces = ["inference"]
  token_policies = [vault_policy.provisioner_rw.name]
}
```

alex: The risky part is we change the path metadata (owner tag) and add the role. I want to avoid any downtime for the HPA/VPA loop. Plan is: apply terraform, update k8s deploys to reference the role, then rotate secret in a single maintenance window.

maria: Sounds fine. Two requests: 1) add a short TTL fallback for the provisioner to read an env var from a fallback secret, 2) add a one-line doc in infra runbook about rollback steps.

sahil: also ensure HPA target metrics server has read perms — it's using a token that mounts the same path for prefix cache keys. If role changes, update `metrics-reader` binding.

alex: good catch. I'll include a quick patch to the HPA HorizontalPodAutoscaler manifest to avoid pod eviction during scaling while keys rotate. Example patch below:

```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: provisioner-hpa
  namespace: inference
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: provisioner
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 60
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
      policies:
        - type: Percent
          value: 20
          periodSeconds: 60
```

jen: if you set scaleDown stabilization to 5m that should reduce flapping during rotation. Also can we add a temporary PDB tweak to keep at least 2 pods available?

maria: agreed. Add this to the PDB: `minAvailable: 2`.

alex: will do. Timeline: I'll push the TF PR now, then wait for +2 approvals, then schedule a 30m maintenance slot tomorrow 02:00 UTC for the rotation. Can infra oncall ack and take post-apply watch?

jen: I'm oncall tomorrow morning and can cover the apply/watch. Please @me in the PR.

sahil: i'll update the `metrics-reader` binding and the rotator job to annotate the canary group. Will ping when done.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: PR opened by alex -> https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pull/842 (labels: infra, critical) :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks everyone. I'll link the PR, add the PDB/HPA changes and the fallback TTL env var, and request approvals. If anyone sees a consumer I'm missing (webhooks, observability), please shout now. :loud_sound:
